name: SQLite
about: SQLite (E1 in docs/dbaba-curriculum.md). Lab-tested on SQLite 3.53 (Python's sqlite3) and the 3.45 command line: its own error messages (the diagnoser), the other databases' words it refuses with their SQLite rewrites, and date arithmetic that runs but means something else. The other query checks are general SQL reasoning until E1's later nights re-check them on SQLite.

notes.limit: LIMIT n OFFSET m works as on MySQL/PostgreSQL.
notes.concat: || joins text (NULL makes it NULL); CONCAT() exists from 3.44 and skips NULL parts.
notes.full_join: RIGHT and FULL OUTER JOIN exist only from SQLite 3.39.
notes.now: date('now') / datetime('now') (UTC) or CURRENT_DATE / CURRENT_TIMESTAMP; there is no NOW().
notes.date_add: Dates are text: date(d, '+7 days'), date(d, '+1 month'); no INTERVAL and no DATE_ADD.
notes.date_diff: julianday(end) - julianday(start) gives days (date - date subtracts the leading numbers of the text).
notes.string_agg: group_concat(col, '-') joins a group's text (string_agg is its other name from 3.44).
notes.identity: INTEGER PRIMARY KEY is the row id and numbers itself; AUTOINCREMENT only stops ids being reused; INSERT ... RETURNING id (3.35+) gives the new id.
notes.upsert: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(col) DO UPDATE / DO NOTHING (3.24+), like PostgreSQL; also INSERT OR REPLACE / INSERT OR IGNORE.
notes.case: = compares case-sensitively; LIKE ignores case for ASCII letters.
notes.types: Column types are only preferences: an INTEGER column accepted 'hello' and kept it as text. Add CHECK (typeof(col) = 'integer') or a STRICT table (3.37+) to refuse it.
notes.division: int / int drops the fraction (7 / 2 = 3), like PostgreSQL.
notes.greatest: No GREATEST/LEAST: max(a, b, c) / min(a, b, c) with several arguments (NULL if any argument is NULL).
notes.boolean: No BOOLEAN type: TRUE and FALSE are 1 and 0.

lab.sql: SELECT CURRENT_DATE IS NOT NULL, datetime('now') IS NOT NULL
SELECT group_concat(x, '-') FROM (SELECT 'a' AS x UNION ALL SELECT 'b')
CREATE TABLE lab_u (n INTEGER); INSERT INTO lab_u VALUES ('hello'); SELECT typeof(n), n FROM lab_u
CREATE TABLE lab_t (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, v TEXT UNIQUE); INSERT INTO lab_t (v) VALUES ('a'); INSERT INTO lab_t (v) VALUES ('a') ON CONFLICT (v) DO NOTHING; SELECT COUNT(*) FROM lab_t
CREATE TABLE lab_i (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, v TEXT); INSERT INTO lab_i (v) VALUES ('a'); INSERT INTO lab_i (v) VALUES ('b') RETURNING id

lab_about: These notes were run on SQLite 3.53 (Python's sqlite3) by tests/practice/test_night10.py; SQLite stays notes-only until it has its own rules.

messages.re: Cannot add a (?P<what>NOT NULL column with default value NULL|PRIMARY KEY column|UNIQUE column)
table (?P<table>[\w$]+) has (?P<want>\d+) columns but (?P<got>\d+) values were supplied|\b\d+ values for \d+ columns\b|all VALUES must have the same number of terms
attempt to write a readonly database
database disk image is malformed|file is not a database|file is encrypted or is not a database

syntax_error:
-- Look just before "{token}": a missing comma, an unclosed ' or (, or words from another database.
-- SQLite has no SHOW TABLES / DESCRIBE (use sqlite_master / PRAGMA table_info), no FOR UPDATE, no INTERVAL, no TOP n (use LIMIT n), no ::casts (use CAST(x AS type)).
-- 'incomplete input' means the statement ends too early: a missing ) or END, or an unclosed quote.
unknown_table: SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type IN ('table', 'view') AND name LIKE '%{table_hint}%';

-- Check which FILE the app opened: a wrong or relative path silently creates a new, empty database.
PRAGMA database_list;
unknown_column: -- Text values go in 'single quotes'; "double quotes" are for names.
ambiguous_column:
-- Put the table (or its alias) in front of the column:
SELECT t1.{column}, ... FROM t1 JOIN t2 ON ... WHERE t1.{column} = ...;
unknown_function:
-- SQLite's own words: NOW() -> datetime('now'), CURDATE() -> date('now'), DATE_ADD(d, INTERVAL 7 DAY) -> date(d, '+7 days'),
-- DATEDIFF(a, b) -> julianday(a) - julianday(b), YEAR(d) -> strftime('%Y', d), DATE_FORMAT -> strftime, LEFT(s, n) -> substr(s, 1, n),
-- LOCATE / CHARINDEX -> instr(s, x), LEN / CHAR_LENGTH -> length, GREATEST / LEAST -> max(a, b) / min(a, b), NVL / ISNULL -> IFNULL
-- Paste the query and say it is SQLite: I'll rewrite each call.
aggregate_misuse:
SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount) AS total
FROM orders
GROUP BY customer_id
HAVING SUM(amount) > 1000;   -- the condition on the total goes in HAVING

-- In UPDATE/DELETE compare with a subquery:
DELETE FROM t WHERE amount < (SELECT AVG(amount) FROM t);
duplicate_key:
-- See the row that already has it:
SELECT * FROM {table} WHERE {column} = ?;

-- Save without failing when it already exists (upsert, SQLite 3.24+):
INSERT INTO {table} ({column}, ...) VALUES (...)
ON CONFLICT ({column}) DO UPDATE SET ... = excluded....;   -- or DO NOTHING
-- INSERT OR REPLACE deletes the old row first: its other columns and its rowid are lost. Prefer the upsert above.
not_null:
-- Send a value for {column} from the app (an empty form field often arrives as NULL),
-- or give the column a DEFAULT: SQLite can't change a column's default with ALTER TABLE, so rebuild the table with it.
fk_missing_parent:
-- Rows that point nowhere, in every table:
PRAGMA foreign_key_check;
bad_value_type:
-- 'datatype mismatch': an INTEGER PRIMARY KEY (the rowid) takes only whole numbers; send one, or leave it out for a new id.
-- 'cannot store ... value in ... column': a STRICT table refusing another type; convert it first, e.g. CAST(? AS INTEGER).
value_count_mismatch:
-- Name the columns and give one value for each, in the same order:
INSERT INTO {table} (col1, col2) VALUES (?, ?);

-- See the table's columns in order:
SELECT name FROM pragma_table_info('{table}');
table_exists: SELECT sql FROM sqlite_master WHERE name = '{table}';
disk_full:
-- Space freed by DELETE stays inside the file until (needs free disk about the file's size):
VACUUM;
db_file_locked:
-- Wait for the lock instead of failing at once (milliseconds, per connection):
PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000;

-- Let readers keep reading while one connection writes:
PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL;
file_readonly:
-- The app's user must be able to write the file AND its folder (SQLite creates a -journal / -wal file next to it):
-- ls -l app.db ; ls -ld <its folder>   then fix the owner or permissions for that user
-- Also check the connection isn't opened read-only (mode=ro in a file: URI).
cannot_open_file:
-- Use an absolute path to a folder that exists and the app can write; a relative path depends on where the app was started.
-- e.g. sqlite3.connect('/srv/app/data/app.db')
file_corrupt:
-- Save what can be read into a new file (sqlite3 command line, 3.29+):
-- sqlite3 broken.db ".recover" | sqlite3 fixed.db
-- 'file is not a database': the path points at another file, or at an encrypted database opened without its key.
alter_not_supported: -- A NOT NULL column can be added with a default: ALTER TABLE {table} ADD COLUMN c TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '';

refuses.title_hi: {db} mein :: cast nahi hota (wo PostgreSQL ka hai)
refuses.fix_en: Use CAST(x AS type), which works on every database.
refuses.fix_hi: CAST(x AS type) likho, ye har database pe chalta hai.

refuses.title_hi: {db} mein :: cast nahi hota (wo PostgreSQL ka hai)
refuses.fix_en: Use CAST(x AS INTEGER).
refuses.fix_hi: CAST(x AS INTEGER) likho.

refuses.title_hi: {db} mein :: cast nahi hota (wo PostgreSQL ka hai)
refuses.fix_en: Use CAST(x AS REAL) for a number with a fraction.
refuses.fix_hi: CAST(x AS REAL) likho.

refuses.title_hi: {db} mein :: cast nahi hota (wo PostgreSQL ka hai)
refuses.fix_en: Use date(x): it gives the YYYY-MM-DD text. (Don't write CAST(x AS DATE) on SQLite: it gives only the year, 2024.)
refuses.fix_hi: date(x) likho (CAST(x AS DATE) SQLite pe sirf saal deta hai).

refuses.title_hi: {db} mein :: cast nahi hota (wo PostgreSQL ka hai)
refuses.fix_en: Use datetime(x): it gives the YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS text.
refuses.fix_hi: datetime(x) likho.

refuses.title_hi: {db} mein :: cast nahi hota (wo PostgreSQL ka hai)
refuses.fix_en: Use CAST(x AS type) with a type SQLite understands (TEXT, INTEGER, REAL, NUMERIC, BLOB).
refuses.fix_hi: CAST(x AS type) likho (TEXT, INTEGER, REAL, NUMERIC, BLOB).

refuses.title_hi: {db} mein ILIKE nahi hota (wo PostgreSQL ka hai)
refuses.fix_en: Use LIKE: on SQLite it already ignores case for the letters A-Z (not for letters like é or ा: compare lower() of both, or use a NOCASE column).
refuses.fix_hi: LIKE likho: SQLite pe ye A-Z ke liye pehle se case ignore karta hai.

refuses.title_en: {db} has no DUAL table (that's Oracle / MySQL)
refuses.title_hi: {db} mein DUAL table nahi hoti
refuses.fix_en: A SELECT without FROM works on SQLite: drop FROM DUAL.
refuses.fix_hi: FROM DUAL hata do: SQLite pe bina FROM ka SELECT chalta hai.

refuses.title_hi: {db} mein SYSDATE nahi hota (wo Oracle ka hai)
refuses.fix_en: Use datetime('now') (in UTC; datetime('now', 'localtime') for the computer's local time).
refuses.fix_hi: datetime('now') likho (UTC mein).

refuses.title_en: {db} has no OFFSET ... FETCH (that's SQL Server / Oracle)
refuses.title_hi: {db} mein OFFSET ... FETCH nahi hota
refuses.fix_en: SQLite pages with LIMIT n OFFSET m (LIMIT first).
refuses.fix_hi: SQLite mein LIMIT n OFFSET m likho (LIMIT pehle).

refuses.title_en: {db} has no FETCH FIRST (that's the SQL standard / Oracle / SQL Server)
refuses.title_hi: {db} mein FETCH FIRST nahi hota
refuses.fix_en: Use LIMIT n at the end of the query.
refuses.fix_hi: Query ke aakhir mein LIMIT n likho.

refuses.title_hi: {db} mein SELECT ... FOR UPDATE nahi hota
refuses.fix_en: SQLite locks the whole database file for a write, not rows: start the transaction with BEGIN IMMEDIATE (it takes the write lock at once), then read and write, then COMMIT.
refuses.fix_hi: SQLite rows nahi, poori file lock karta hai: transaction BEGIN IMMEDIATE se shuru karo, phir padho-likho, phir COMMIT.

refuses.title_hi: {db} mein INSERT IGNORE nahi hota (wo MySQL/MariaDB ka hai)
refuses.fix_en: SQLite says INSERT OR IGNORE. Like INSERT IGNORE it skips rows that break UNIQUE, NOT NULL or CHECK rules, not only duplicates; ON CONFLICT (col) DO NOTHING skips only that conflict.
refuses.fix_hi: SQLite mein INSERT OR IGNORE likho (ye bhi duplicate ke alawa NOT NULL / CHECK todne wali rows chhod deta hai).

refuses.title_en: {db} has no ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE (that's MySQL/MariaDB)
refuses.title_hi: {db} mein ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE nahi hota
refuses.fix_en: SQLite's upsert is ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET, and the new row's values are excluded.col (MySQL's VALUES(col)). Without a column list after ON CONFLICT it needs SQLite 3.35+; name the unique column, ON CONFLICT (email), for older versions.
refuses.fix_hi: SQLite ka upsert ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET hai, aur nayi row ki value excluded.col (MySQL ka VALUES(col)).

refuses.title_en: {db} has no VALUES(col) in an upsert (that's MySQL/MariaDB)
refuses.title_hi: {db} mein upsert ke andar VALUES(col) nahi hota
refuses.fix_en: The new row's value is excluded.col on SQLite.
refuses.fix_hi: SQLite pe nayi row ki value excluded.col hai.

refuses.title_hi: {db} mein TRUNCATE nahi hota
refuses.fix_en: DELETE FROM t with no WHERE empties the table (SQLite does it quickly). An AUTOINCREMENT counter keeps counting unless its row in sqlite_sequence is deleted too.
refuses.fix_hi: Bina WHERE ka DELETE FROM t table khaali karta hai.

refuses.to: SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'table' ORDER BY name
refuses.title_hi: {db} mein SHOW TABLES nahi hota
refuses.fix_en: The tables are listed in sqlite_master (the command line also has .tables).
refuses.fix_hi: Tables sqlite_master mein milti hain (command line pe .tables).

refuses.title_en: {db} has no DESCRIBE / SHOW COLUMNS (that's MySQL/MariaDB)
refuses.title_hi: {db} mein DESCRIBE nahi hota
refuses.fix_en: PRAGMA table_info(t) lists the columns, their types, NOT NULL, defaults and the key.
refuses.fix_hi: PRAGMA table_info(t) columns dikhata hai.

refuses.error: near the alias or JOIN: syntax error
refuses.title_hi: {db} mein UPDATE ... JOIN nahi hota
refuses.fix_en: Write UPDATE t SET col = ... FROM other WHERE other.key = t.key (SQLite 3.33+), or SET col = (SELECT ... FROM other WHERE other.key = t.key) on older versions.
refuses.fix_hi: UPDATE t SET col = ... FROM other WHERE other.key = t.key likho (SQLite 3.33+).

refuses.error: near the table name: syntax error
refuses.title_en: {db} has no DELETE t FROM t JOIN ... (that's MySQL/MariaDB)
refuses.title_hi: {db} mein DELETE t FROM ... JOIN nahi hota
refuses.fix_en: Write DELETE FROM t WHERE key IN (SELECT t.key FROM t JOIN other ON ... WHERE ...).
refuses.fix_hi: DELETE FROM t WHERE key IN (SELECT ...) likho.

refuses.title_en: {db}'s ALTER TABLE can't change a column
refuses.title_hi: {db} ka ALTER TABLE column nahi badal sakta
refuses.fix_en: SQLite's ALTER TABLE only renames, adds or drops (3.35+) columns. To change a type, default or NOT NULL, rebuild the table: CREATE TABLE t_new (...), INSERT INTO t_new SELECT ... FROM t, DROP TABLE t, ALTER TABLE t_new RENAME TO t, all in one transaction with foreign keys off.
refuses.fix_hi: SQLite ka ALTER TABLE sirf naam badalta, column jodta ya hataata hai. Type badalne ke liye table dobara banao (nayi table, rows copy, purani drop, rename).

refuses.title_hi: {db} mein REGEXP apne aap nahi hota
refuses.fix_en: SQLite parses REGEXP but has no function behind it unless the app adds one (Python: conn.create_function('regexp', 2, ...)). For simple patterns use LIKE ('a%' starts with a) or GLOB ('[0-9]*' starts with a digit, case-sensitive).
refuses.fix_hi: SQLite mein REGEXP ka function app ko jodna padta hai. Saade patterns ke liye LIKE ya GLOB likho.

refuses.title_hi: {db} mein DIV nahi hota
refuses.fix_en: CAST(a / b AS INTEGER) keeps the whole part, toward zero, as DIV does (lab: 7 DIV 2 = 3, -7 DIV 2 = -3 on MariaDB and the rewrite on SQLite).
refuses.fix_hi: CAST(a / b AS INTEGER) likho (DIV ki tarah poora hissa).

refuses.title_en: {db} has no MOD operator word (that's MySQL/MariaDB)
refuses.title_hi: {db} mein MOD shabd nahi hota
refuses.fix_en: Use a % b. On SQLite % works on whole numbers (7.5 % 2 is 1.0, not 1.5): for fractions use mod(a, b) where the math functions are built in (3.35+).
refuses.fix_hi: a % b likho (SQLite pe % poore numbers pe chalta hai).
